pairs.difference: A: the ball's shade is cut up by panel. The blue panel holds the dark group, with white panels beside it and a small black pool at the contact point. That grouping is closer to the real lesson cards. Key and contrast are almost identical, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Light the ball from one side so the whole lower-left of the ball falls into one soft shadow across all panels and joins the cast shadow; keep the sand smooth and calm, without bright speckle.

pairs.difference: B: the white target rings against the dark red panel give a hero-background gap of 0.159, just past the real ceiling. A solid black strip fills the bottom under the shelf and the side walls fall to dark, so the darkest area is large and sits at the card edge rather than on the hero. A: mid-dark panel, bright bulbs in an arc, and the blue disc's dark side keeps the target within the mid range. The black stays in small pockets under the shelf.
pairs.fix: Remove the black band under the shelf and make it a warm mid-tone wood; lift the side walls; keep the deepest darks to small contact shadows beside the target and bear.

pairs.difference: B: the card is the brightest of the pair at 0.753, well above the real top of 0.707. Its lower-left and ceiling corners go near white, so the corners are lighter than the centre (vignette -0.047). The unit merges with the bright wall as one white mass, and a hard black slit in the vent is the only dark. A: also high key, but the corners darken and the left wall sits in shade, framing the white unit with a soft mid-tone blue side.

pairs.difference: B: bright sand and pale glowing water put the card at a higher key. The chest is cut out by crisp, even light rims on every metal strap, and a solid black lid interior sits against them, so local contrast on the hero is hard and spread evenly. A: dark blue background, with the lid's top band as the one big light and the body held in soft middle and dark greys. Its value edges are softer.
pairs.fix: Deepen the water to a rich mid-dark blue, lower the sand's brightness, keep only one big light on the lid, and let the metal straps on the front fall into mid-tone shade without bright rims.

pairs.difference: B: the overall key of 0.50 sits below every real card (lowest 0.55). The upper wall is a near-black striped mass with streaky dark grain, and the hat's badge and band are lost in a black block, so dark takes a large area at the top edge. Corners read lighter than the centre (vignette -0.040). A: the wall is an even mid-dark, the white crown is one large light, and the black is limited to the band and peak.
pairs.fix: Raise the back wall to a warm mid-tone wood with no near-black planks, make the whole scene brighter, and keep the deep darks only under the peak and band of the cap.

pairs.difference: A: corners do not darken (vignette -0.043, below the real low of -0.010). The back wall breaks into blotchy patches of two greys at upper right and upper left, with no clean glow shape, and a near-white floor pool sits low in the card. B: one clean round glow behind the booth, a steady background group, and the booth is one dark mass against it.
pairs.fix: Put a single soft round glow behind the booth and let the wall fade evenly darker toward all four corners; make the wall a smooth even tone without blotches, and lower the floor's brightness.

pairs.difference: B: heavy one-sided falloff. The right wall drops to dark while the left stays lighter (vignette -0.103, far below the real low of -0.030), so the background group is uneven. Thin bright and dark stripes add hard wall edges, and black pools pack under and between the gloves. A: three simple groups: flat mid wall, light floor, dark gloves. Highlights are gentle and the corners are level.
pairs.fix: Light the wall evenly from left to right in one mid-tone with soft stripes, remove the thin dark and bright lines, and keep the shadow under the gloves soft and mid-dark rather than black.

pairs.difference: B: the yellow blades sit in one flat light-grey group with no white, and the only strong dark is the black foot pockets, so the form reads as inflated and evenly lit. A: the blades go to white with a clear fall to mid-tone and small black accents at the blade tips, giving a fuller range on the hero. Both are slightly darker in key than real cards, so the numbers do not separate them.
pairs.fix: Let the top of each yellow blade reach a bright near-white highlight that rolls down to deeper yellow in shade, and add small dark accents at the tips where the blade edge turns under.

pairs.difference: A: key 0.737 is above the real top of 0.707, and contrast 0.119 is under the real floor of 0.124. Sky, sea and sand all sit in light greys with near-white foam at the bottom, and the pier is a thin mid-grey with no dark group, so the card has no real dark mass. B: a deep water mass, a dark post and a bright sand corner give clear light, middle and dark shapes.
pairs.fix: Deepen the sea to a rich dark teal around the pier, lower the foam and sand brightness, and give the wooden posts a dark shadow side so the pier stands out as the darkest mass.

pairs.difference: B: the pink background is a single flat mid-grey with no corner falloff or visible ring structure in value. The sand goes to a broad near-white, and the fronds break into scattered light and dark slivers. A: darker corners with a lighter ring glow behind the crown, a clear mid-toned sand and a solid cast shadow, so the groups are simpler. Contrast is low on both cards.
pairs.fix: Add a soft lighter glow behind the palm crown with corners falling clearly darker, lower the sand from near white to warm mid-light, and give the palm a solid soft cast shadow on the sand.

pairs.difference: A: corners are lighter than the centre (vignette -0.055, below the real low of -0.030). The left wall carries a big dark shape from the cast shadow, the upper right stays pale, and the floor breaks into streaky white. B: steady wall tone with level corners, a tidy white skirting band, and the deep darks held inside the locker.

pairs.difference: A: key 0.732 is high and contrast 0.109 is under the real floor of 0.12. The tiles are a broad near-white, the green slide sits in light and mid greys with thin bright edges, and only small darks remain on the supports. B: the slide has broad dark undersides that form a large shadow shape on the coil, set against a lighter wall.
pairs.fix: Lower the tile floor to a soft mid-light tone and give the slide's underside and inner curves broad, deep green shadow so the coil reads as one bold dark and light shape.

pairs.difference: A: the gap of 0.223 is the widest in the pair and well above the real top of 0.128. The player is nearly all white in five-grey, with only tiny value steps at the buttons, and it sits on flat, hard-edged background rings. B: also over the range at 0.203, but the player's body falls from a lit top to a clearly darker lower face, with a soft shadow beneath it. This is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Let the lower half and right side of the player fall into a deeper orange shade, soften the background rings, and add a soft shadow under the device so it is not one flat bright shape.

pairs.difference: B: high key at 0.78 and contrast of 0.094 near the real floor. The background is a bright, even green with little corner fall, and the envelope is one blank white mass with almost no dark accent, so hero and background separate more by hue than by value. A: corners go dark, the background has a stepped glow behind the hero, and the envelope gains clear value separation against it.

pairs.difference: B: mid-light wood fills the card with no big value shapes, and the plate holds many small scattered darks at the seeds, berries and gaps, so contrast of 0.115 falls under the real floor. A: bold light stripes behind a darker cluster of fruit, giving a clear hero-versus-background gap of -0.148, though the key of 0.754 runs slightly high.
pairs.fix: Set the fruit against a simple lighter background with a broad soft glow, gather the dark fruits into one group at the base of the plate, and calm the wood grain to one smooth tone.

pairs.difference: B: the wall goes to a near-white at the card edges, so the corners are far lighter than the centre (vignette -0.138, well past the real low of -0.071). The door is a dark, evenly toned cut-out in a bright frame. A: also has a negative vignette, near the bottom of the real range, but the door fills the card as one big dark group, with the white flowers as the single light accent.
pairs.fix: Bring the wall down from near white to a warm mid-tone and let the outer edges of the card fall darker, so the blue door and wreath stay the brightest, clearest area in the centre.

pattern: Generated cards still show themselves through an evenly lit, high-key hero and an unmanaged card edge. Corners often run lighter than the centre (negative vignette), or a wall falls off to one side instead of a clean glow with darker corners. Keys and contrast drift out of the real range. Some cards go pale with low contrast and no real dark mass; others carry a large black band or wall at the card edge. Darks and highlights are scattered as many small crisp accents and bright rims, where real cards keep one broad shadow side, simple light, middle and dark groups, and soft roll-off into shade. Separation margins are small, so most calls are low to moderate confidence.
